It's the currency that other nations hold in their central bank reserves.
The currency used to price global commodities.
The currency that international trade is denominated in.
When you're the reserve currency, every country needs your money.
To buy oil, they need your currency.
To settle trade imbalances, they need your currency.
To hold safe assets, they need your bonds.
This creates something called exorbitant privilege.

It's why empires fight to achieve it and why they collapse when they lose it.

Stage one. Military dominance and trade route control.
Every reserve currency begins the same way, with overwhelming military power that controls
critical trade routes, not just having a strong military, controlling the pathways that global
commerce flows through. In the 1450s, Portugal achieved something unprecedented. They mastered
oceanic navigation. While other European nations were still hugging coastlines,
Portuguese sailors were crossing open oceans. They rounded the Cape of Good Hope in 1488.
This opened a sea route to Asia that bypassed the Ottoman-controlled land routes,
and they militarized this advantage. Portuguese warships dominated the Indian Ocean,
the South China Sea and the Atlantic. They established fortified trading posts at strategic
